articleTitle: Accelerated life testing of electrical insulation with generalized life distribution function
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: A new approach to estimating the life distribution of electrical insulation at nominal conditions from the results of accelerated life testing of electrical insulating materials is introduced by the authors. A very general family of probability distributions is introduced and a best fit member of this family is used to represent lift data at each stress level. Nonlinear optimization techniques are applied in conjunction with linear regression analysis. A numerical example based on actual test data of insulating material and a user-friendly computer program are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A stochastic load model for use in operating reserve evaluation
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The authors present an analytical model of the short-term load that includes, in addition to the expected load, the expected variation. The variation is important because it is this variation of the load (together with potential unit failures) that causes operational risk. The authors present a general Gaussian stochastic sequence load model; explain why it is a reasonable model; and show how this model can be estimated from empirical data that should be available with any type of short term load forecast. Finally, the authors approximate the stochastic load model by a Gauss-Markov sequence, the Markov property greatly simplifies evaluation of unit commitment risk due to both unit failures and load variation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of a composite system reliability program for large hydrothermal power systems-issues and solutions
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The authors describe a new computational tool, called NH2, for composite reliability evaluation. The system state selection methodology is based on successive enumeration or Monte Carlo simulation. The system performance analysis is carried out by an algorithm that includes: state configuration, pre-solution, solution, monitoring and a specially designed LP-based remedial actions model. The approach is illustrated in case studies with a 660-bus system derived from the Brazilian Southern/Southeastern (SSE) system. It is shown that composite outages have a substantial share in the SSE system. The program can be run on standard PC microcomputers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Probabilistic load modelling for power system expansion planning
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The authors present a more realistic load modelling to probabilistic load flow when applied to power system expansion planning. The Brazilian North-Northeastern system load data are used to model the short and long-term peak load uncertainties.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A Monte Carlo simulation model for adequacy assessment of multi-area generating systems
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The authors illustrate a Monte Carlo simulation procedure for adequacy assessment of multi-area generating systems. A sequential approach based on the state residence times of generating units and tie lines is utilized. The model uses the maximum flow algorithm to calculate power interchanges between areas when a load loss situation is found in one or more areas. The duty cycle of peak load units can be accurately modelled using chronological representation of the system component operating cycles. Load forecast uncertainty can also be included. The frequency and duration indices can be estimated and the distributions of various reliability indices obtained. The model is illustrated by comparison between analytical answers and simulated values for a single area IEEE-RTS. Studies are then extended to several multi-area configurations constructed by connecting many IEEE-RTSs together.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Importance sampling for power system security assessment
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: A Monte Carlo simulation scheme for estimation power system network failure rates has been developed and implemented. It uses an importance sampling strategy which biases the simulation sample towards the extreme conditions leading to loss of supply. A theoretical analysis of the performance of the sampling scheme is given, and numerical experiments both with an idealised 3-node network and 22-node model of the UK South-West peninsula 400 kV network confirm predictions of large improvements in efficiency, compared with standard Monte Carlo sampling runs using 1000 simulations suffice to determine system failure rates to within 5-10%. Similar gains in efficiency are obtained using a demand disconnection index of system failure, rather than a simple fail/no fail criterion.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A hybrid algorithm for Monte Carlo/enumeration based composite reliability evaluation (power systems)
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The authors discuss possible hybrid schemes for combining enumeration and Monte Carlo approaches in composite reliability evaluation. One intuitive approach is to use enumeration to select transmission contingencies, followed by Monte Carlo sampling for the generation contingencies. It is shown that this technique can be seen as a stratified sampling scheme. Computational experiments with a 124-bus system derived from a Brazilian configuration indicated that this hybrid scheme was not attractive, even if the optimal strata allocation and optimal ranking schemes were used. The basic reason seems to be that the contributions of transmission contingencies to composite reliability indices, when combined with generation contingencies, are not concentrated in a few 'severe' outages, but are 'spread out' in a more or less uniform way. Further experiments with other systems are required before these conclusions are generalized. Finally, it is pointed out that the so-called variance reduction schemes can be seen as hybrid schemes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reliability assessment of the operational functions of a power system control center
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The reliable operation of the facilities at a system control center (SCC) is essential to the secure and economical operation of a modern power system. Ontario Hydro's new SCC is designed to carry out several sets of functions, such as real-time monitoring, security and economic assessments of system operations, etc. The author demonstrates the application of probability methods to assess the overall reliability of the SCC facilities in carrying out these functions. The computed performance indices were compared with a set of specified targets. The selection of SCC functional reliability indices and performance targets, the reliability assessment approaches, and the results of the assessment are summarized.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Security considerations in composite power system reliability evaluation
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The composite power system has been classified into different operating states in order to recognize security considerations in the system reliability assessment. Annualized indices obtained by considering the load to be constant throughout the year and the annual indices by considering a seven-step load model have been presented. A basic electric power utility objective should be to operate in the normal state with high probability. A system may be capable of operating within constraints but may not be able to withstand outages, even single level. A risk index designated as CSOSR (composite system operating state risk) has been defined and the utilization of this CSOSR for a simple system expansion plan has been demonstrated. It has been shown that composite reinforcement with both generation and transmission gives better results than simple addition of either generation or transmission facilities in the case of the MRBTS. This CSOSR is a new risk index which can be used in a wide variety of system studies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A classification of failures of the protection
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The authors look at the different aspects of the reliability of the electricity supply. To find the relations between reliability, protection and design, they propose a classification of failures of the protection. The proposed classification distinguishes between failure of the concept; failure of the model; failure of the setting; and failure of the device.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Probabilistic assessment of short-circuit currents in large power systems
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: Short-circuit currents have by nature a multi-variable stochastic character affected by probabilistic conditions, like the fault location in the network, the type of the fault, the fault impedance and the prefault state of the system. The proposed method takes into account the random nature of these conditions using conditional probabilities and provides an analytical expression for the short-circuit current distribution with a minimum of assumptions. Thus, not only the worst case probability but also the probability of each occurrence is obtained. This increased amount of information can be extremely valuable for an objective decision-making. As a result, not only considerable savings in capital investment can be achieved, but more important designs with known risks, reliability and with sufficient margins of safety can be produced.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Probabilistic approach of voltage control based on structural aspect of power systems
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: In this paper, the author presents the probabilistic concept of voltage electrical distance, and clearly demonstrates the central role in classification selection of subsystems for voltage control and as a measure of the uncertainty in the voltage variation in proximity to nonmonitored nodes. The author believes that this concept may find application in areas, and further researches are leading to definition of a distance for transient stability.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Determination of thermal line ratings from a probabilistic approach
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The author calculates line ratings by quantifying the risks associated with given load currents, having regard to the random nature of weather parameters. Probabilistic ratings are defined as the constant load currents corresponding to a given probability, in terms of cumulated frequency, of not exceeding the design temperature.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Probabilistic methods for assessing harmonic power losses in electricity distribution networks
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The author gives guidelines for probabilistic estimation of combined harmonic power and energy losses caused by a number of harmonic sources. The harmonic producing loads and the network impedances are assumed to be known. Methods are proposed for assessing the combined losses taking into account the phase angle and amplitude variation range of the harmonics.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Probabilistic analysis of weather related loads on overhead transmission lines in Ontario, Canada
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: Design and installation of transmission lines are considerable economic undertakings for electric utility companies. The common approach to the design of transmission lines has been by deterministic methods. However, the designers are now considering the use of probabilistic methods to improve the reliability and economics of new transmission lines. The major requirements for applying the probabilistic methods are well established load and strength databases. A program developed previously by the authors (1988) has been used to estimate weather related loads needed for reliability based design of transmission lines. Statistical parameters such as mean, coefficient of variation and Gumbel extreme value coefficients for wind, ice and wind-on-ice loads have been calculated for 30 weather stations in Ontario. Also discussed are the combined occurrences of wind and ice loads on conductors, which would be useful in the probabilistic analysis of certain type of transmission line problems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Composite system reliability assessment using a Monte Carlo approach
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The authors describe some of the basic modeling concepts of a computer program developed for composite generation and transmission system reliability assessment. The program names MECORE is based on a hybrid approach of Monte-Carlo simulation and an enumeration technique. Novel characteristics of the MECORE program are that multi-derated-states of generating units can be considered, effects of regional weather differences can be recognized, impacts of bus load uncertainty and correlation can be simulated and practical load curtailment philosophies are incorporated in the linear programming minimization model used to evaluate a system state in order to obtain realistic bus indices. Calculation results for two test systems (the IEEE Reliability Test System and a small test system developed at the University of Saskatchewan) and relative analyses associated with considering derated states of generating units, regional weather effects and impacts of bus load uncertainty and correlation are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Load forecast uncertainty consideration in generating unit preventive maintenance scheduling for single systems
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: One basic element in power system planning is the determination of how much generating capacity is required to give a reasonable assurance of satisfying the load requirement. The authors present a new technique based on the statistical moments and cumulants for incorporating load forecast uncertainty into the algorithm for maintenance scheduling in single systems. The proposed algorithm has been implemented in a fast and flexible computer program which has been applied to the IEEE Reliability Test System (RTS) and the Saskatchewan Power Corporation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Probabilistic methods applied to harmonic distortion
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The authors have investigated the application of probability theory to two separate problems of power system harmonic distortion: traction and background distortion. In both cases the techniques have followed extensive measurement programs and have been verified against site tests. Agreement between theory and practice is good for the cases studied and the techniques could be extended to further loads. However, this should only follow appropriate testing to derive the basic data. Probabilistic techniques are beginning to be accepted for certain types of distorting load and for the assessment of particular problems. This acceptance should become more widespread as computing and measurement techniques improve.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A probabilistic approach to distribution system reliability assessment
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PGE), together with California Polytechnic State University in San Luis Obispo, has developed a personal computer program for evaluating the reliability levels of their electric distribution circuits. The program, called the Distribution Reliability Assessment Model (DREAM), incorporates historical outage information with circuit component failure rates and estimates of fault response and component repair times to compute expected levels of customer outage frequency and duration. The authors highlight recent enhancements to DREAM which allow for the evaluation of both overhead and underground circuits. The authors also describe their efforts to measure the accuracy of the DREAM calculations and the application of the program in predicting the reliabilities of 180 feeders.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The practical application of life cycle costing to the design of power systems
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The designer of any new power system-be it generating plant, a transmission re-enforcement or an extension to a distribution system, needs to be confident that the option selected for implementation has been carefully considered against a range of criteria. These criteria are likely to include high reliability, low maintenance and running costs, minimal deleterious effects on current assets and low environmental impact with the need to provide the new asset at the lowest possible cost. To assist in understanding the relationship of the often conflicting criteria on the solution as a whole a total cost model can be used. A total cost model provides the designer with the tool to prepare a life cycle costing for each option being considered. The author demonstrates how such an optimisation can be tackled and how difficulties (i.e. poor data) can be overcome. Finally, an application of life cycle costing, using a commercially available cost optimisation tool is shown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electric power capacity planning under uncertain conditions
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: A dynamic model for electric power capacity expansion planning under uncertain conditions has been developed. The model determines an expansion plan which gives a minimum for the expected total costs in electricity production. Decision sequences are presented in the form of decision trees. Uncertain factors are defined in the form of discrete probability distributions. Certain constraints in the optimization problem are relaxed through Lagrange multipliers and the resulting problem is solved using a decomposition technique. The application of the model to analyse alternative construction policies for Finnish power capacity under uncertain conditions has been discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A continuous probability distribution for generating capacity reliability evaluation
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: There are two broad categories of methods for generating capacity reliability evaluation. The traditional approach is based on obtaining generation capacity probability distribution by unit addition algorithms and convolving it with a suitable load model to obtain indices for generation reliability. The alternative approach used approximation of the discrete probability distribution by a continuous probability distribution. The techniques described in the available literature use some type of infinite expansion based on some well known distributions. The authors propose a different approach by using a multi-parameter probability distribution which by itself, without any expansion terms, provides a close approximation to the exact results. The distribution is a composite of gamma-distributions. Equations for obtaining the distribution parameters from the unit parameters are derived. When the number of parameters is increased, the accuracy of indices is enhanced and the results remain stable.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Probabilistic costing of transmission services
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The adoption of appropriate pricing strategies for the costing of bulk power transmission services is important in the economic operation and development of multi-utility power systems. In particular, both the restructured UK power supply system and inter-utility power wheeling in other systems, requires the application of use-of-system costing in order to promote the economic operation and optimal development of the power system. The authors describe a methodology that has been developed for the costing of the use of bulk transmission services. The approach adopted employs marginal cost pricing for the use-of-system and takes into account the probabilistic nature of the power system arising from uncertainties in generator availabilities.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Assigned- and demand-energy units in probabilistic production costing
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The algorithm presented by Manhire and Jenkins (1982) for probabilistically simulating the operation of power systems which includes multiple assigned-energy units has been extended by the authors. Such assigned-energy units are conventional hydroelectric power plants and, under certain circumstances, nuclear units or conventional thermal units with limited fuel supply or with limits on emissions due to environmental considerations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reliability-based design of transmission lines: a comparison of the ASCE and IEC methods
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: Several reliability-based design techniques for transmission lines have been proposed since the mid 1970s. Out of these proposals, the ASCE and IEC documents have received the most attention and are now available for trial use. With the ASCE procedures, individual components (tower member, connection, foundation, etc.) can be sized to meet or exceed a target reliability level. The resulting effect on the reliability of the entire line, while briefly discussed, is not quantified. With the IEC procedures, the reliability of the entire line is targeted. However, the document is not specific about the design of individual components. The authors discuss the similarities and differences between the two procedures and provide suggestions for improvements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Relationships between components, structures, and line reliabilities
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: A number of reliability-based design methods for transmission structures have been proposed in recent years both in the US and abroad. Two of these proposals have gained wide attention: the ASCE guide and the IEC document, both of which are now available for trial use. Approximate relationships are given between the reliabilities of the line, of individual supporting structures within the line, and of components within a supporting structure. As illustrated through numerical examples, these relationships supplement the ASCE guide and allow system-reliability-based design (SRBD) of a transmission line.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A probabilistic approach to the long-term planning of public electricity distribution networks
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: A new methodology for the long-term planning of public electricity distribution networks is presented, The methods developed take into account both the uncertainties related to the growth of loads and the dynamic nature of the problem. The basic methods used are stochastic dynamic programming and statistical decision analysis. By using the proposed approach, the optimal investment strategy for the long-term development of a distribution network can be evaluated. The methods presented are applied to medium-voltage (e.g. 20 kV) networks, which are radially operated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Statistical determination of unit commitment risk level
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The authors estimate the unit commitment risk level of a practical generating system using operational reserve assessment methods. The estimated risk level may help the Jordan Electricity Authority in applying a probabilistic reliability constraint when trying to find the optimal solution of the unit commitment problem.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Evaluation of a static VAr compensator effect on system reliability using a probabilistic approach
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: Static VAr systems can improve the reliability of a system by increasing transient stability margins. The authors formulate the problem of investigating transient stability improvements due to static VAr compensators as a probabilistic stability problem, in which several aspects that affect system stability are considered: the probability of the fault, the probability of fault location, the probable performance of the protection system and the load variation curve. The authors determine the improvement in reliability margins attributable to a given static VAr compensator installation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Risk engineering the widespread overhead distribution system
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The authors demonstrate the application of probabilistic risk techniques to a widespread overhead electricity distribution system. Specifically, the intention is to show how the logic of conditional probabilities can be combined with the statistical distribution of extreme values and Monte Carlo simulation to model the elements of failure.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Probabilistic approaches to transmission line thermal ratings
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The utilisation of overhead line ratings enhanced as a result of statistical considerations has brought significant benefits and suggests further enhancements are possible. Weather parameters and, more particularly, derived overhead line current carrying capabilities cannot be represented accurately by 'standard' distributions. Differences in weather around the country may permit the enhancement of ratings in some areas. The use of weather forecasts to predict temporary increases in ratings and thereby relax some of the transmission constraints on economic generation dispatch is a possibility which merits investigation. The feasibility of the concept will largely hang on a probabilistic risk/benefit analysis.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Probabilistic evaluation of power supplies for large computer and communications installations
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: Reliability analysis is an important tool in the design of power supply systems for large computer/communications installations. A study recently undertaken involved the analysis of such an installation. The authors describe in general terms the approach adopted in the study including the standards set for the quality and availability of electrical power to be delivered to the technical facilities and the probabilistic methods employed in the evaluation of the relevant reliability indices. Lifetime operations and support (maintenance) are also covered as essential components of the assessment. The authors demonstrate that the statistical analytic techniques which are well established in other fields are also applicable in the field of power systems reliability and availability specification and assessment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reliability assessment of mixed hydro thermal systems using sequential simulation
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: Evaluation of the required amount of generation capacity to ensure adequacy of supply is an important factor during both the planning and the operation stages of a power system. There are two basic reliability evaluation methods; the analytical approach; and the stochastic simulation approach. Simulation techniques can be divided into two; random and sequential. The sequential approach is particularly justified when the system states at any given point in time are partially determined by the historical evolution of the system. The authors describe the application of simulation techniques to the reliability evaluation of hydro-thermal generation systems. They include a review of the models and the techniques. Analyses of two systems are discussed; the first is the IEEE Reliability Test System (RTS), and the second is based on a real Spanish hydro system. The effects of using different operation and management policies are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modelling of scheduled maintenance for power system planning
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The authors describe the ESCORT maintenance model which produces realistic simulations of numerous operational situations. User interaction is required to obtain a satisfactory set of rules and post-fault limits, but this can give valuable insight into future system operation. Numerical details of unsupplied energy and out of merit costs do not always compare accurately with operational reality, but the reasons are understood and the values remain useful for planning purposes. Ways of ameliorating the run time problem have been described and satisfactory performance demonstrated for a 74 line sub-system. The program is well established as a planning tool and is valuable in the hands of an experienced user.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Scheduling of generating units maintenance under uncertainty
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: In a problem of generating units maintenance scheduling usually both the objective function and constraints are formulated as the linear functions. The author explains how the division of planning horizon into discrete time intervals allows one to solve this optimization problem with the use of linear integer programming methods. The dimension of the problem depends upon the number of generating units destined for maintenance and the number of elementary time intervals.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A reliability data base for performance and predictive assessment of electric power systems
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The authors present an overview of the CEA reporting procedures for assessing overall power system performance and providing generation, transmission and distribution outage statistics which can be used to predict future performance. The equipment Reliability Information System (ERIS) is presented with particular emphasis on the ability of the system to provide the necessary reliability parameters to support the conventional models used in reliability evaluation. The Electric Power System Reliability Assessment (EPSRA) procedure is briefly described. This procedure, when fully implemented, should provide an extremely important source of comparative utility performance data.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reliability and security assessment of existing transmission lines using fuzzy set theory
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: A new method for updating reliability and security of existing transmission lines is introduced. In this method, the uncertainty is divided into objective and subjective parts. The objective part can be processed by probability theory. The subjective part is dealt with by fuzzy set theory. Two fuzzy sets for each subjective factor, one for gravity of the subjective feature and the other for the effect on the event of interest are formed using linear membership functions. Fuzzy intersect is then used to merge the gravity and the effect of each subjective factor. To merge the objective and subjective information, a fuzzy conditional relation is formed and the composition of this relation with the subjective information is made. From the composition, a fuzzifier subset is extracted and the objective information is fuzzified.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Probabilistic estimation of the capacity of drilled shaft foundations
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: A method is proposed for estimating the undrained capacity of drilled shaft foundations subjected to static uplift loads such as power overhead lines. The method accounts for random variability of soil properties, uncertainty in measurements, and inaccuracies in empirical correlations between in-situ measurements and design soil properties. A full probabilistic description is specified for the foundation capacity. This description depends on several uncertain parameters that can be estimated from soil data.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The influence of primary energy uncertainties on probabilistic load flow
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The authors propose a new set of procedures that integrates primary energy uncertainties and energy operating policies with probabilistic load flow. The reservoir operational strategies are then considered in the assessment of adequacy indices. The proposed methodology is applied to two examples related with the Brazilian power network. Comparisons are made between this approach and the deterministic strategy. Topics requiring further developments are also mentioned.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Load combinations in EHV transmission line design
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The authors discuss the results of an analysis undertaken to determine limit states, design wind loads and temperature effects for EHV transmission lines for the South African Electrical Power Authority, Eskom, and presents a framework for extending this approach to safety and security loads. This approach is based on reliability principles, taking into account the likely combination of different loads.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Investigation on the treatment of generating unit outages in probabilistic production simulation
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The authors report the results of an investigation on several treatments of generating unit random outages in probabilistic production simulation. An electric utility system with a mix of nuclear, coal, and gas-fired generating units and a peak load of about 5000 MW was used in the investigation. The authors also describe the treatment of the unit random outages, the utility system, simulation results and conclusions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Probabilistic overload assessment in distribution networks
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The developed program Pronet is a menu-driven computer program for probabilistic overload assessment of distribution networks. The program combines a deterministic N-1 contingency analysis with a more realistic probabilistic approach, which can save network investments and maintenance costs. The authors describe the method of calculation used for probabilistic overload indices and the used models used for load, network and reliability. The graphic output is presented in some examples. The assessment of the overload risk is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A probabilistic theory of lightning incidence with application to overhead line protection
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The author looks at direct lightning hits to shield wires and conductors of overhead power lines. The random nature of lightning incidence is analysed using probability theory. Closed form approximate expressions are derived for the rate of back-flashovers and shielding failure flashovers as functions of the critical current and tower geometry.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Comparison of alternative techniques for the reliability assessment of distribution systems
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The authors illustrate two alternative methods for distribution system reliability evaluation. The first method developed at UMIST in conjunction with UK's electricity supply industry and second developed at University of Sarajevo in conjunction with Yugoslavian electricity supply industry. The reliability results predicted by the two methods, for the two practically based distribution systems, are very close. The authors also describe and demonstrate different sensitivity studies such as: effects of alternative design characteristics, different failure and restoration modes, environmental factors and the effect of PLOC events by two alternative methods.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Probabilistic transformer reserve
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The transformer capacity reserve in a substation has been established in the Brazilian utilities by using qualitative criteria like substation size, voltage level and operational experience. This criterion, that can lead to a noneconomic configuration motivated the development of a probabilistic methodology to determine the transformer capacity reserve of substations composed of single-phase and three-phase transformer banks. The authors describe the probabilistic method and the economical benefits achieved.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The probabilistic rating of separate pipe cooled cables
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: To protect cable insulation, a temperature limit needs to be imposed on cables during operation. Since heat generated in the cable is mainly current dependent, this limit translates into a current limit which represents the current rating of the system. The authors report on a study carried out on a 400 kV separate pipe cooled underground cable system conventionally rated at 2038 A in winter and 1972 A in summer. Results of the probabilistic analysis giving the temperature profile of the system for December and July are presented. In addition, temperature limits for 20% and 30% overload conditions and the effects of varying water flow rates and inlet temperatures are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reliability analysis of industrial electricity supply
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The high interruption costs associated with modern industrial plants, calls for a highly reliable electricity supply. In order to weigh installation costs against interruption costs, a quantification of reliability is needed. One of the methods to obtain reliability parameters like expected number of interruptions and duration of interruption is a Monte Carlo simulation. Therefore the power system in question is divided into components for which the fall and restore behaviour is known. The statistical behaviour of each component is simulated, as well as the relation between the state of the components and the state of the complete system. Observations on this simulation system will give estimates of the reliability parameters. All this is contained within a computer program.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A comparative study of power generation system reliability including the consideration of energy limited units
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: Recently, attention has been given to reliability evaluation of generation systems including the effect of energy limitations. The basic methods are the forced outage rate (FOR) modification technique; the load modification approach based on the load duration curve; and the F and D (frequency and duration) method based on the cumulative load model and equivalent load method. In the latter two models, the operating condition of the energy limited units is characterized by a peak shaving method (PSM). In the FOR modification method, the effect of unit's energy limitation is reflected by modifying the unit forced outage rate and treating the energy limitation as an equivalent failure. The author presents the results of a comparative study of these methods. Illustrative examples and the IEEE-RTS system are used and reliability induces are computed for comparison of these models.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Calculating the expected unserved energy in generating systems using the concept of mean capacity outage
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The authors present the concept of mean capacity outage by means of which the calculation of the expected unserved energy in generating systems can be reduced to a straightforward summation over the chronological load data. Unlike existing methods the proposed method does not require construction of a negative margin table. The proposed method is illustrated by application to a small sample-system and to the IEEE Reliability Test System.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer aided maintenance for distribution lines: an expert system approach of failure risk evaluation
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The authors describe an expert system based on electrical network failures risk evaluation. This application is directed to give a sorted list of electrical distribution network components to repair or to renew, given a technological and environmental context for each component. After a presentation of the system, the authors detail the risk evaluation carried out by the expert system and compare it to classic reliability approach. Advantages of the expert system approach are underlined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reliability of vacuum switching equipment
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The authors demonstrate new analytical methods for designing and evaluating vacuum switching equipment. The reliability engineering approach achieves higher reliability and reduces production cost. The transition from former experience science to reliability engineering results in economic, safe, and reliable operation of systems that are complicated in structure. Current advanced computer technology provides convenient calculation methods for solving the huge amount of data. Reflecting these trends, a reliable and realistic approach in designing and evaluation of mechanical elements has been developed for products, in the field that have operational and failure data records. This database supplies reliable data and optional design information on mechanical components.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of spread footings-probabilistic analysis of full scale testing results
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: In the period 1955-63 the Electricity Supply Board, Ireland (ESB) carried out a series of 61 tests on full scale foundations to ascertain the parameters to be used in the design for uplift of foundation sizes then in use. In the period 1984-7 the ESB set and tested a total of 54 full-scale foundations in three different locations in Ireland in a variety of soil conditions using different methods of installation. A further 14 foundations from a 40 year old line were tested in 1988. The site testing and statistical analysis of results of these foundation tests forms the basis for this paper which suggests design parameters to be used for the principal soil types, foundation shapes and dimensions examined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An analytical approach to probabilistic uncertainty and sensitivity analysis (for power systems)
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: An analytical method, called APUA, to calculate the properties of an algebraic function of random variables in a power system is presented. The principle of the method is briefly described and compared to other techniques. Two examples of application are presented. The results are compared to those given by Monte Carlo simulation and first-order Taylor series. The method seems to give reasonable results and it can be used to estimate the total uncertainty caused by many variables or by a subset of them.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A probabilistic production cost model with optimization of the loading order
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The authors present a new power system probabilistic production cost model developed as a benchmark to establish comparisons with classical production cost models. The importance of the operating constraints and loading order optimization has been emphasized. The impart in the utilization factors of the units, as a consequence of the assumptions made in probabilistic simulation models, has been evaluated and shown to be very significant in certain cases. Illustrative numerical results have been presented using a realistic example based on the Spanish electric system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reliability-based design of overhead transmission structures-a critical review
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The application of reliability-based methods for the design of transmission structures is gaining wide-spread recognition as a viable alternative to the existing deterministic approaches. The Electric Power Research Institute (EPRI), the American Society of Civil Engineers (ASCE) and the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) have proposed different approaches to apply reliability-based design methods to transmission lines. Ontario Hydro has a long-term program to develop its own version of reliability-based design method. The EPRI, ASCE and IEC methods are briefly reviewed to compare the differences and similarities between them. The three methods are then applied to a real high voltage transmission line in Ontario. Also discussed is the outline of a proposed new reliability-based design method for transmission lines.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Wood pole strength data base for reliability-based design
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: For the past decade or so, Ontario Hydro has been involved in developing Reliability-Based Design (RBD) methods for the design of transmission and distribution lines. A sound database is essential for the successful application of the RBD design methods. Ontario Hydro's program to develop a database for strength of wood poles is described and the limited data collected to date is statistically analyzed. The application of these statistical parameters to calculate strength factors for reliability-based design is briefly discussed. The use of nondestructive evaluation technique to establish database for wood pole strength is also described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Assessment of electric service reliability worth
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The basic function of a modern electric power system is to satisfy the system load and energy requirements at the lowest possible cost, while maintaining an adequate degree of continuity and quality of supply. Establishing the worth of service reliability is a difficult and subjective task. Direct evaluation is not considered feasible, and an approach that is evolving is to evaluate the impacts and monetary losses resulting from electrical supply interruptions, which is, in effect, the societal cost of unreliability. These interruption costs are not considered equal to the reliability worth, but merely a surrogate of it. The authors provide a survey of the range of methods used to evaluate reliability worth or costs of unreliability (outage costs) as reported in the literature. The general evolving trends of the various methods are summarized and the customer postal survey method is identified as the method preferred by utilities.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Operational and expansion planning of Brazilian systems based on probabilistic load flow
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The authors present some applications of the probabilistic load flow (PLF) program FLUXP, to assist the decision-making process utilized in operations and expansion planning studies. The main features of this program are discussed together with the indices that can be obtained. Two examples are given to demonstrate the potential of the PLF technique to deal with both operational and expansion planning problems. Both large interconnected Brazilian networks, South/Southeastern and North/Northeastern, are used. The authors also present a concise analysis of the economical benefits resulting from the application of the PLF technique as well as the rationale for the establishment and validation of the numerical criteria utilized. Finally, a number of computational and modelling hurdles and the corresponding envisaged solutions are also highlighted.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Probabilistic bulk production cost model by a continuation Monte Carlo simulation method
publicationTitle: 1991 Third International Conference on Probabilistic Methods Applied to Electric Power Systems
abstract: The authors present a novel approach that attempts to drastically reduce the computation cost of Monte Carlo simulations of bulk power systems, without sacrificing modelling detail regarding network representation or chronology. The approach borrows both from techniques based on the continuation method, and from ideas germane to LP parametric programming. The method has been specifically designed to be used with power systems of large dimensions; however, so far it has been only tested at a prototype level. The emphasis of this paper is on the presentation of the theoretical aspects of the proposed approach.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
